summary: ```# How to Make a Bow in Marvelous Designer? - A Step-by-Step Guide to Creating a Bow! ## Introduction Hello everyone! Today, we are going to learn how to make a butterfly knot in Marvel's The Santa. This tutorial will guide you step-by-step through the process of creating a beautiful bow. ## Step 1: Prepare the Virtual Model 1. **Open the Dress**: First, we need to open this dress in the preview and put it on any virtual model. 2. **Adjust Model Properties**: In the attribute editor, reduce the surface diameter of the virtual model to 1. This will make the clothes closer to the virtual model. 3. **Select Dress Panels**: Select all dress panels and reduce their particle diameter to 10. Then, copy it using the control key. This step is crucial to prevent the butterfly knot and the smaller panel from merging, which may cause instability. ## Step 2: Freeze Dress Panels - **Freeze Panels**: Freeze all the dress panels and start to create the butterfly knot. ## Step 3: Create the Butterfly Knot 1. **Make a Rectangle**: First, create a rectangle. This rectangle will serve as the ear of the butterfly knot we will make later. 2. **Apply New Fabric**: Select this panel to apply new fabric. 3. **Merge Panels**: Merge the rectangular side to the front and middle of the collar. 4. **Switch to Line Knot Tool**: Switch to the line knot tool by pressing the shortcut key `N`. Merge the same side of the line, keeping in mind that these two panels are folded. 5. **Change Knot Type**: Change the type of knot for this set to "Turned." ## Step 4: Simulate and Adjust - **Simulate**: Simulate by pressing the control key. After opening the simulation, you can manually drag this pattern around. - **Create Fixed Needle**: Press `W` to click on the pattern and create a fixed needle. Use the fixed needle to flatten it in three-dimensional space. - **Adjust Particle Diameter**: Reduce the particle diameter of the ear of the butterfly knot to 10 and the conflict thickness to 1. ## Step 5: Delete Fixed Needle - If you want to delete the fixed needle, press `W` to click again to delete it. However, if it is not fixed, the pattern may collapse gently, making it inconvenient for further work. ## Step 6: Shape the Rectangle - **Check Shape**: Check the shape of the rectangle created in the video. You can see its specific length by using the edit sheet tool to select one edge. Since the butterfly knot will have two layers, this layer belongs to the inside and needs to be turned over on the surface. ## Step 7: Fold and Simulate 1. **Open the Sheet**: Click on the outer edge of the sheet in 3D space and find the corresponding line in the 2D window to open this sheet. 2. **Create a Fold**: Now we have the outside of the butterfly knot. Create a line in the middle to fold. 3. **Use Fold Arrangement Tool**: Go to 3D space, use the fold arrangement tool to select this inner line, and drag the arrow on the corresponding side to fold the sheet over. 4. **Simulate Again**: Press the control grid button to open the simulation. ## Step 8: Harden and Finalize the Knot - **Harden the Sheet**: The butterfly knot material is relatively soft; first, harden the sheet to fold. After starting the simulation, you can see the hardened sheet and its folding effect is very obvious. - **Adjust Particle Precision**: Step the particle precision of the butterfly knot to 5 for better simulation effects. - **Sew the Knot**: Press the shutter button to switch to the line division tool and connect the two sides of the butterfly knot. Since the lines on both sides are folded, switch the line type to "Turned." ## Step 9: Final Adjustments 1. **Simulate and Remove Hardening**: After folding the board and sewing it, remove the hardening to prevent the butterfly knot from falling. 2. **Add Fixing Pins**: Press the `W` key and click the corner of the butterfly knot board to add fixing pins at the corner position. 3. **Activate Collar Board**: To make it easier for us to create the knot of the butterfly knot later, activate the collar board and simulate it together. ## Step 10: Draw Internal Lines - **Internal Lines**: To make the butterfly knot look more realistic, draw some internal lines in the middle and set the folding angle to fold the middle. Use the internal multidirectional line tool to draw a foldable internal line, referencing the position of the internal line in the 3D window. ## Conclusion After following these steps, you should have a beautifully crafted butterfly knot that can be used in your designs. Don't forget to check the effect of the butterfly knot and make any necessary adjustments. Thank you for watching this tutorial! Feel free to experiment by adding some butterfly decorations to your clothes. See you next time! ```
